title: What is a Market? Adventure
welcome_lead: Markets are everywhere — online, in shops, even in school. 🏬
meta_desc: Customers & Markets Adventure 1 — KS3 Business Studies on what markets are and the different kinds.
final_note: You learned what a market is and met several common types.

concepts.def: Buying and selling on the internet
A small, specialised group of buyers

walkthroughs.body_html:
A market is anywhere buyers meet sellers.

It could be a stall, a high street shop, eBay or TikTok Shop. 📱

A local market is nearby — Saturday market in town.

A global market reaches buyers worldwide — Amazon ships to over 100 countries.

The internet has turned tiny businesses into global ones.

A niche market is small but special — like left-handed scissors or vegan trainers.

Fewer customers, but they pay more for something made just for them. 🎯

options: CSR is purely about being ethical with no business benefit.
CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.

Reasons include genuine ethics, but also commercial benefits — improved reputation, customer loyalty, employee retention, and reduced regulatory or reputational risk.

mcqs.q: What is Taylor's theory of scientific management?
options: Taylor said workers are motivated by recognition and teamwork.
Workers are motivated primarily by money; efficiency is maximised by breaking tasks into standardised steps, training workers in 'the one best way', and using piece-rate pay.
Taylor invented the assembly line at Ford.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.

mcqs.q: What are the four Ps of the marketing mix?
options: Product, Price, Place (distribution), and Promotion — the controllable variables a business uses to satisfy customers and achieve objectives.
The four Ps are Product, Price, Profit, and People.
CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.
